This option follows the pattern.

Option (3): 191 : 177

Now, follow the logic:

191 – 177 = 14

This option do not follow the pattern.

Option (4): 797 : 679

Now, follow the logic:

797 – 679 = 118

This option follows the pattern.

Hence, pair “191 : 177” is an odd one.

Alternate Method The logic followed here is:-

Sum of digits of first number - Sum of digits of second number = 1

1) In 727 : 609

Sum of digits of first number = 7 + 2 + 7 = 16

Sum of digits of second number = 6 + 0 + 9 = 15

Sum of digits of first number - sum of digits of second number → 16 - 15 = 1

2) In 373 : 255

Sum of digits of first number = 3 + 7 + 3 = 13

Sum of digits of second number = 2 + 5 + 5 = 12

Sum of digits of first number - sum of digits of second number → 13 - 12 = 1

3) In 191 : 177

Sum of digits of first number = 1 + 9 + 1 = 11

Sum of digits of second number = 1 + 7 + 7 = 15

Here, sum of digits of second number > Sum of digits of first number

Also, Sum of digits of second number - sum of digits of first number → 15 - 11 = 4

4) In 797 : 679

Sum of digits of first number = 7 + 9 + 7 = 23

Sum of digits of second number = 6 + 7 + 9 = 22

Sum of digits of first number - sum of digits of second number → 23 - 22 = 1

questions.q: Who among the following was one of the leaders of the Santhal rebellion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sidhu Manjihi.

Key Points

• Santhal Rebellion took place during Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856) tenure at Rajmahal hills (in Jharkhand) led by Sidhu Manjhi.

• Santhal uprising took place during 1855-56.

• The tyrannical British revenue system, usury practices, and the zamindari system in India made Santhal peoples annoyed, and two Santhal brothers Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu organized 10,000 Santhals and proclaimed a rebellion against the British.

• The Santhals are the largest tribal group in India found in Jharkhand, WestBengal, and Odisha.

• Santhal Rebellion:

• It was a rebellion against both the British colonial authority and zamindars by the Santhal people.

• Leaders: Sidhu, Kahnu, Chand, and Bhairav.

• Location: Jharkhand.

• The rebellion was suppressed and largely shadowed by other rebellions.

• To quell rebellion British created Santhal Pargana and special laws were

passed protecting them.

Additional Information

• Britishers invited the Santhals to come and settle in Jharkhand promising land and economic amenities.

• Thus Santhals from different states came to settle in today's Jharkhand.

• Later zamindars dominated these areas as they collected taxes and lent money at very high rates which the people could not generally pay and their lands were forcibly taken.

• This became the roots of the Santhal rebellion.

• In a fierce encounter, Santhals were defeated as they were fighting with bows and arrows while Britishers had modern weapons.

• Sidhu was caught in August 1855 and was hanged on a banyan tree at a place called Panchkathia.

• It is one of the most important Himalayan passes in the country. Nathu means 'listening ears', and La means 'pass'.

• It is one of the three open trading border posts between India and China and is famous for its picturesque beauty and beautiful environment.

• Nathu La is located on the Old Silk Route. It is a mountain pass in the Himalayas in the East Sikkim district.

• It connects Sikkim to China's Tibet Autonomous Region. It was sealed for almost 4 decades after the People's Republic of China suppressed a Tibetan uprising in 1959.

• The Nathu La Pass was reopened in 2006 and since then, it has served as an official Border Personnel Meeting(BPM) Point.

questions.q: Who among the following was the first Indian to win a seat in the House of Commons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

Key Points

• First Indian elected to the British House of Commons, Dadabhai Naoroji contested on the ticket of Liberal Party.

• Dadabhai Naoroji was also known as the "Grand Old Man of India" and "Unofficial Ambassador of India".

• He was an Indian political leader, merchant, scholar and writer who was a Liberal Party Member of Parliament in the United Kingdom House of Commons between 1892 and 1895.

• Naoroji is honoured for his work in the Indian National Congress, of which he was one of the founding members and thrice - in 1886,1893, and 1906 - elected president.

• His authored book Poverty and Un-British Rule in India brought attention to his theory of the Indian "wealth drain" into Britain.

• India Post showing Naoroji on stamps in 1963, 1997 and 2017.​

Additional Information

• Liberal Party:

• Liberal Party, a British political party that emerged in the mid-19th century as the successor to the historic Whig Party.

• It was the major party in opposition to the Conservatives until 1918, after which it was supplanted by the Labour Party.

• The Liberals continued as a minor party until 1988 when they merged with the Social Democratic Party to form what is now called the Liberal Democratic Party.

• Through its long history, the Liberal Party included various schools of thought, but all Liberals were united by the conviction that the source of progress lay in the free exercise of individual energy.

• Labour Party:

• Labour Party, a British political party whose historic links with trade unions have led it to promote an active role for the state in the creation of economic prosperity and in the provision of social services.

• In opposition to the Conservative Party, it has been the major democratic socialist party in Britain since the early 20th century.

• In 1900 the Trade Union Congress (the national federation of British trade unions) cooperated with the Independent Labour Party(founded in 1893) to establish a Labour Representation Committee, which took the name Labour Party in 1906.

• Conservative Party:

• Conservative Party, byname Tories, in the United Kingdom, a political party whose guiding principles include the promotion of private property and enterprise, the maintenance of a strong military, and the preservation of traditional cultural values and institutions.

• Since World War I the Conservative Party and its principal opponent, the Labour Party, have dominated British political life.

• The name Conservative was first used as a description of the party by John Wilson Croker writing in the Quarterly Review in 1830.

• Communist Party:

• The Communist Party of Britain (CPB) is a communist political party in Great Britain idealized to Marxist-Leninist theory.

• The party came out from a dispute between Eurocommunists and Marxist-Leninists in the Communist Party of Great Britain in 1988.

• Ex-members included General Secretaries of three organisations:

• Bob Crow of the RMT union, Ken Gill of the Manufacturing.

• Science and Finance (MSF) union and member of the TUC General Council.

• Kate Hudson of the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament (CND).

Given:

The boat takes 25 mins to go 5 km downstream and 2.5 km upstream

Concept used:

When going downstream, the speed of the boat and the flow of the river are added to calculate the net speed.

When going upstream, we take the difference between the speed of the boat and the flow of the river as the net speed.

Distance = Time × Speed

Elimination method for solving linear equations

Calculation:

Let the speed of the boat and the flow of the riven be B & R respectively. (in Kilometer per hours i.e. kmph)

Now,

Upstream speed = B - R = 1/P (suppose)

Downstream speed = B + R = 1/Q (suppose)

45 mins = 3/4 hour

25 mins = 5/12 hour

According to the question,

5/(B - R) + 7.5/(B + R) = 3/4

⇒ 5P + 7.5Q = 3/4 ....(1)

According to the question,

2.5/(B - R) + 5/(B + R) = 5/12

⇒ 2.5P + 5Q = 5/12 ....(2)

Solving (1) & (2) we get,

Q = 1/30 i.e. 1/(B + R) = 30

Now,

B + R = 30

The net speed during downstream = 30kmph

Now,

Time taken to cover 6km downstream

⇒ 6/30 hour

⇒ 1/5 hour

⇒ 1/5 × 60 mins

⇒ 12 mins

∴ 12 mins will it take to go 6 km downstream.

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In any right angled triange like above

a = √(b² + c² - d²)

In the question, we have b = 11, c = 8 and d = 13

So, a = √(112 + 82 - 132)

Given:

AQ = 11cm

PC = 8cm

AC = 13cm

Concept used:

Pythagorean theorem states that the sum of the squares on the other two sides of a right-angled triangle is equal to the square on the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle)

Calculation:



Let the length of AB, BC, BQ & PB be T, S, x & y respectively.

Now,

ΔABC, ΔABQ, ΔBPC and ΔPBQ are all right-angled triangles.

From ΔABC,

⇒ S² + T² = 13² ....(1)

From ΔABQ,

⇒ x² + T2 = 112 ....(2)

From ΔBPC,

⇒ y² + S2 = 82 ....(3)

From ΔPBQ,

⇒ x2 + y2 = PQ2 ....(4)

Adding (2) & (3),

x2 + T2 + y2 + S2 = 112 + 82

⇒ x2 + y2 + (S2 + T2) = 185

⇒ x2 + y2 = 185 - (S2 + T2)

⇒ x2 + y2 = 185 - 169

⇒ x2 + y2 = 16

⇒ x2 + y2 = 4²

⇒ PQ² = 4² (From 4)

⇒ PQ = 4 (∵ Negative value can't be consider for length)

∴ The length of PQ is 4cm.

A. He was in the habit of stealing food from others.

B. One night, the villagers decided to teach him a lesson and kept only rotten food in their kitchen.

C. The culprit ended up eating the rotten food and fell sick.

D. Once upon a time, there lived a man in a village.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'DABC.'

Key Points

• The sentence 'D' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "a man in a village". Hence, 'D' is the first part.

• Sentence A will come after D as it is giving information about the habit of the man (stealing from others).

• Sentence B will come after A as it is explaining what the villagers decided to do with the man one night (they decided to keep rotten food for the man).

• The sentence 'C' is the concluding part because it is giving information about what finally happened with the man after eating rotten food.

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences: *Once upon a time, there lived a man in a village. He was in the habit of stealing food from others. One night, the villagers decided to teach him a lesson and kept only rotten food in their kitchen. The culprit ended up eating the rotten food and fell sick*.

Hint

• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:

• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.

• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).

• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

Hinglish

• वाक्य 'D' किसी अन्य वाक्य से स्वतंत्र है क्योंकि यह "एक गांव में एक आदमी" के बारे में सामान्य जानकारी दे रहा है। अतः 'D' पहला भाग है।

• वाक्य A, D के बाद आएगा क्योंकि यह आदमी की आदत (दूसरों से चोरी) के बारे में जानकारी दे रहा है।

• वाक्य B, A के बाद आएगा क्योंकि यह समझा रहा है कि ग्रामीणों ने एक रात उस आदमी के साथ क्या करने का फैसला किया (उन्होंने आदमी के लिए सड़ा हुआ भोजन रखने का फैसला किया)।

• वाक्य 'C' समापन भाग है क्योंकि यह इस बारे में जानकारी दे रहा है कि आखिरकार सड़ा हुआ खाना खाने के बाद आदमी के साथ क्या हुआ।

Key Points

• The present perfect tense format 'Subject + have + V3 (done) + Object' will be changed into the past perfect tense format 'Subject + had + V3 (done) + Object'.

questions.solution:

Key Points

• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.

• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.

• The given sentence is in the active voice and it is in the past simple tense.

• When we convert this sentence into a passive voice, the subject ''Shiva'' of the active voice becomes the object, the object ''a letter'' becomes the subject.

• The active format "V2 (wrote)" should be converted into the passive format "was + V3 (written)".

• This is the active and passive voice rule for the past simple tense.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Directions: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If there is no error, select ‘No error ’ as your answer.

questions.solution:

Key Points

• In the given sentence, the plural form of the verb ''live'' is incorrect.

• The subject 'brother' in the given sentence is a singular subject.

• The singular form of the verb 'lives' should be used with the singular subject 'brother'.

• Therefore, the singular form of the verb ''lives'' should be used in place of the plural form 'live'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *My brother who lives in Pune is arriving tomorrow*.

Additional Information

• Subjects and verbs must agree with one another in number (singular or plural). (विषय और क्रिया एक दूसरे के साथ संख्या (एकवचन या बहुवचन) में सहमत होना चाहिए)

• Thus, if a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if the subject is plural, its verb must also be plural. (इस प्रकार, यदि कोई विषय एकवचन है , तो उसकी क्रिया भी एकवचन होनी चाहिए ; यदि विषय बहुवचन है , तो उसकी क्रिया भी बहुवचन होनी चाहिए)
